time_map.why: 0:00.6-0:11.5 (score 0-10, bars 1-5): the quiet col legno opening. The alignment only locks on at bar 6; before that it started the ostinato 0.9s late and wandered (user, Nov 17: 'the start is VERY inconsistent, and not lining up'). The recording's bar downbeats come every 2.17s from the first attack at 0.58 (onsets 0.58, 2.75, 4.95, 7.11, 9.29, 11.49), the written rhythm at a steady tempo.

two_hands.why: 1:11-1:24 (score 67-78): the trumpets' 78 and the euphoniums' 67 (with the horns from 69.2) trade back and forth over the horns' held 71. Played with both hands: right = trumpet, left = euphonium/horn, each note held while the other answers (user, Nov 18). The rules can't tell a call and response from two parts doubling.

lead_part.why: 3:02-3:13 (score 168-178): the trumpets take up the figure the euphoniums started two beats earlier (72 72 72 | 72 71 72 72 71 72 | 75 72 72 75 ...): the trumpets are the line on top, and every repeated note is struck (user, Nov 18: 'missing a lot of the start notes after holds, where the first note is the same as the held note'). The theme-returns rule was handing these bars to the horns' held 68, and the held-over-reattack rule then swallowed the repeats.

2:42.9-2:43.5 (score 150-150.8): the woodwinds' 83 (doubled by the first violins) starts the phrase 83 80 80 83 85 88 ...; the rules pick the fourth horn's 66 66 under it -- a chord-filling part, not a repeated note, so the tune-over-repeated-notes rule doesn't apply (user, Nov 18: 'locking onto the low brass background').
